Case :- Criminal Appeal No. - 6347 of 2019
Appellant :- Anil Kumar Vishwakarma

Respondent :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Appellant :- Ajay Pandey,Anil Kumar,Mohit Singh

Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ram Manohar Narayan Mishra,J.
Order on Bail Application Notice has reportedly been served on the informant as per the communication of CJM, concerned, dated 9.12.2021.
But none appeared on behalf of the informant.
Heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned AGA for the State.

As this appeal arises out of impugned judgement and order dated 26.9.2019 passed by Special Judge (POCSO Act), Kaushambi in Criminal Case No. 104 of 2016 (State vs. Anil Kumar Vishwakarma),
Case Crime No. 119 of 2016, under Sections 363, 366, 376(2)(Jha) IPC and 3/4 POCSO Act, P.S.
Charwa, District Kaushambi, convicting the appellant under Section 363 IPC and sentencing him to undergo imprisonment for five years imprisonment with fine of Rs. 5,000/-; for charge under Section 366 IPC to undergo for five years imprisonment with fine of Rs. 5,000/-; for charge under Section 376(2)(Jha) IPC to undergo for 11 years imprisonment with fine of Rs. 11,000/- and for charge under Section 4 of POCSO Act to undergo 12 years imprisonment with fine of Rs. 12,000/-
with default stipulation; all the sentences were directed to run concurrently; the bail application of the appellant is being disposed of by this order:

sentences.text: As per the prosecution version, appellant enticed away the victim, who is daughter of informant, aged around 12 years on 17.6.2016 at 8:30 AM; she was kept by accused in a hotel at Allahabad for five days and she was subjected to rape by the accused; victim has stated her age to be 13 years in statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. whereas in Madarsa record, her date of birth is mentioned as 7.1.2007; in the medical examination report, her age is found as 14 years.

Learned counsel for the appellant submits that he has been falsely implicated in this case; story of pregnancy and miscarriage has not been substantiated by any medical evidence and learned trial court has also not placed reliance on that version of the victim; her testimony recorded before the trial court is not in consonance with previous statements; as per custody certificate, appellant has undergone actual period of sentence 6 years one month 9 days till 6.8.2022, therefore, she has undergone more than six years 7 months actual imprisonment till date.

Learned counsel submits that the appeal may take some time for its final disposal and in the light of the judgement passed by Supreme Court on 25.02.2022 and 09.05.2022 in the case of Saudan Singh vs. State of U.P. in Criminal Appeal No. 308/2022 arising out of SLP (Crl.) No. 4633 of 2021 and in Suleman Vs. The State of Uttar Pradesh (Misc. Application No. 764 of 2022 in Crl. Appeal No. 491 of 2022), respectively, the appellant is entitled to be released on bail.

sentences.text: The State counsel opposes the bail application and submits that though on merits appellant does not have a good case but he is not in a position to dispute the detention period of the appellant.

Considering the totality of the case, in particular, detention period of the appellant and the fact that the appeal may take some time for its final disposal, without further commenting on the merits of the case, this Court is inclined to release the appellant on bail.

Let appellant, Anil Kumar Vishwakarma, convicted and sentenced in the above mentioned sessions trial, be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 50,000/- (Fifty Thousand) and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned.
On acceptance of bail bond and personal bond, the lower court shall transmit photostat copies thereof to this Court for being kept on the record.
List this appeal for final hearing in its due course.
In the meanwhile, Registry to prepare paper book, if not already prepared.
It is made clear that half of the fine awarded under the impugned judgement shall remain stayed subject to deposit remaining half of the fine within one month after being released on bail.
